title: When they go quiet
hook: When they go quiet, separate evidence from the story your anxiety writes.
body_or_script: Silence can feel like an answer, but it is often just an empty space your mind tries to fill. Before you act, write down what you know, what you are guessing, and what pattern has repeated.
caption: When they go quiet, do not let anxiety write the whole story. Private Love Test in bio.

title: The three-column pause
hook: Before you send the next message, use the three-column pause.
body_or_script: Put facts in one column, feelings in the second, and needs in the third. The next message should come from your need for clarity, not from panic.
caption: The next text lands better when you know what you actually need.

title: One silence is not a verdict
hook: One silence is not a verdict. A pattern is something you can name.
body_or_script: One silence may hurt. A repeated silence tells you something different. The useful move is not to panic. It is to notice whether the pattern gives you clarity, repair, or only more guessing.
caption: Notice the pattern before you turn silence into a verdict.

title: What evidence do you actually have?
hook: What evidence do you actually have, and what story did anxiety add?
body_or_script: Ask yourself: what did they actually do, what did I add on top of it, and what would help me feel clear without abandoning myself?
caption: If the story grew faster than the evidence, pause before action.
